# Varyn

Varyn is a vulkan-based modular live shader coding tool. You can attach modules to each other and organize your shaders much better than a single file. The tool was completely made using Claude Code along with my edits here and there.

## Modularity

Varyn features a multi-file structure where you can include a series of modules you've made before.

```glsl
#include <varyn.glsl>     // generated by Varyn: uniforms, textures, vertex inputs
#include "lighting.glsl"  // your own module, found next to the shader or in include_dirs
```

## Features

- Live shader coding and auto reload on file changes (shaders, modules, config, textures and models)
- Configuration through a TOML config file
- Every value in the config can be an expression of `time`, e.g. `fov = "60 + 10 * sin(time)"`
- Importing 3D models and configuring their scale, rotation and position
- Shaders get `time`, `deltaTime` and `frame`, plus camera matrices and your own uniforms
- Compile errors are printed and the last working shader stays on screen

## Building

Requirements: a C++20 compiler, CMake ≥ 3.24, GLFW 3.3+, GLM, stb_image, and the
LunarG Vulkan SDK (for the shaderc library). [toml++](https://github.com/marzer/tomlplusplus)
is downloaded automatically by CMake.

```sh
source ~/vulkan/<version>/setup-env.sh   # optional: CMake also finds ~/vulkan/* on its own
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja
cmake --build build
```

## Running

```sh
./build/varyn examples/varyn.toml
```

More examples in `examples/`:

| Config            | Shows                                                               |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `varyn.toml`      | the sample scene: instancing, expressions, textures, metallic models |
| `mandelbrot.toml` | the same scene on a zooming Mandelbrot floor                        |
| `juggler.toml`    | a figure made of spheres juggling chrome balls, with cast shadows (`[[models.passes]]`) and shader glints, animated purely with expressions in honor of Eric Graham's 1987 Amiga Juggler Demo |

| Option           | Effect                                                     |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--validation`   | Enable the Vulkan validation layer                         |
| `--print-header` | Print the generated `varyn.glsl` for a config and exit     |

| Key   | Action                                  |
| ----- | --------------------------------------- |
| Space | Pause / resume time                     |
| R     | Restart time and frame count            |
| F5    | Reload everything                       |
| Esc   | Quit                                    |

## Config reference

Paths are relative to the config file. **Any number can also be a string
expression** (see [Expressions](#expressions)). Vectors can be written as a
single value to fill every component, e.g. `scale = 2`.

```toml
[window]
title = "Varyn"
width = 1280
height = 720
vsync = true
clear_color = [0, 0, 0, 1]

[shaders]                            # required
vertex = "shaders/main.vert"
fragment = "shaders/main.frag"
include_dirs = ["modules"]           # where #include "x.glsl" looks

[camera]
position = ["5 * sin(time)", 2, "5 * cos(time)"]
target = [0, 0, 0]
up = [0, 1, 0]
fov = 60                             # vertical, degrees
near = 0.1
far = 100

[[textures]]                         # becomes `uniform sampler2D <name>`
name = "albedo"
path = "textures/albedo.png"
filter = "linear"                    # or "nearest"
wrap = "repeat"                      # or "clamp"

[uniforms]                           # 1-4 values -> float / vec2 / vec3 / vec4
speed = 2.0
color = [1, "0.5 + 0.5 * sin(time)", 0.2]

[uniforms.orbit]                     # an array: `vec3 orbit[4]` in shaders, element i
count = 4                            # evaluated with i = 0..count-1 and n = count
value = ["2 * cos(time + i / n * tau)", 1, "2 * sin(time + i / n * tau)"]

[[models]]
name = "ship"
path = "models/ship.obj"             # an .obj file ...
# builtin = "cube"                   # ... or a builtin: quad, cube, sphere
# vertex / fragment = "..."          # optional per-model shader override
metallic = 0.8                       # 0..1, reflects the scene (see below)

  [[models.instances]]               # one entry per placement
  position = [0, "sin(time)", 0]
  rotation = [0, "time * 45", 0]     # degrees, applied X, then Y, then Z
  scale = 1

  [[models.instances]]               # `count` copies, using i = 0..count-1 and n = count
  count = 8
  position = ["3 * cos(i / n * tau)", 0, "3 * sin(i / n * tau)"]

  [[models.instances]]               # position, rotation or scale may name a 3-component
  count = 4                          # uniform to reuse its expressions, so shaders and
  position = "orbit"                 # models share one definition

  [[models.passes]]                  # draw every instance again with other shaders,
  vertex = "shaders/shadow.vert"     # e.g. flattened onto the floor as a shadow;
  fragment = "shaders/shadow.frag"   # each stage defaults to the model's own
```

`metallic` may be an expression and can use `i` / `n`. Every instance of a
model with this option gets an environment cube map, captured each frame from
the instance's position with that instance left out (6 extra scene renders per
instance, 256×256 per face). Shaders read it with `sampleEnvironment()`; the
example `lighting.glsl` module wraps that in `shadeMetallic()`. Reflective
instances see each other one frame late.

Without any `[[models]]`, Varyn draws a single fullscreen quad with the default
shaders, which makes it a classic fragment-shader playground.

### Expressions

| Kind      | Available                                                                            |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Variables | `time` (or `t`), `dt`, `frame`, `i`, `n` (instances only), `pi`, `tau`, `e`          |
| Operators | `+ - * / %`, `^` (power), unary `-`, parentheses                                     |
| Functions | `sin cos tan asin acos atan atan2 sqrt abs floor ceil fract round sign exp log`      |
|           | `pow min max mod step clamp mix smoothstep radians degrees`                          |

## Shader interface

`#include <varyn.glsl>` declares everything Varyn provides. Run
`varyn --print-header <config>` to see the exact header for your config.

| Name                                       | Type      | Notes                                   |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `time`, `deltaTime`                        | float     | seconds                                 |
| `frame`                                    | int       | frames since start                      |
| `resolution`                               | vec2      | framebuffer size in pixels              |
| `view`, `projection`, `viewProjection`     | mat4      | from `[camera]`                         |
| `cameraPosition`                           | vec3      |                                         |
| `modelMatrix`                              | mat4      | per instance (push constant)            |
| `modelIndex`, `instanceIndex`              | int       | which model / instance is being drawn   |
| `metallic`                                 | float     | the model's `metallic` option, 0..1     |
| `sampleEnvironment(dir)`                   | vec3      | fragment only: the scene reflected in   |
|                                            |           | world direction `dir` (black if none)   |
| your `[uniforms]` and `[[textures]]`       |           | by the names given in the config        |
| `inPosition`, `inNormal`, `inUV`           | vertex in | vertex shader only                      |

The macros `VARYN_VERTEX_SHADER` / `VARYN_FRAGMENT_SHADER` are defined per stage,
so one module can serve both (see `examples/modules/surface.glsl`).

Clip space Y points up (as in OpenGL), depth is 0..1, and output is written
to a UNORM swapchain, so the colour you write is the colour you see.

## Source layout

| Path                           | Responsibility                                           |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/App`                      | window, clock, file watching and reloads, keys           |
| `src/Config`                   | TOML → `Config` structs                                  |
| `src/Expression`               | parser and evaluator for config expressions              |
| `src/ShaderCompiler`           | GLSL → SPIR-V with shaderc, module includes              |
| `src/UniformLayout`            | std140 uniform layout and the generated `varyn.glsl`     |
| `src/Mesh`                     | OBJ loading and builtin meshes                           |
| `src/FileWatcher`              | timestamp polling                                        |
| `src/render/Scene`             | GPU meshes and textures for a config                     |
| `src/render/Renderer`          | descriptors, pipelines, per-frame drawing                |
| `src/vulkan/`                  | instance/device, swapchain, buffers and images           |
